elements.text: defines the change control process which is implemented in GOTrack within Boehringer Ingelheim (excluding GOTrack eCC – electronical Change Control).

Employes who perform change control, impact assessments for change control, action items for change control as well as employes in Quality who approve change or particular steps and any other employee who approves changes or particular process steps as stake holder or SME
All areas where changes are processed under GxP or equivalent regulations affecting

items: Computerized systems which includes computer systems, spreadsheets, equipment, utilities, facilities

The manufacturing, quality control and distribution* of medical devices, drug device combinations, drug products, vaccines and drug substances as well as any components thereof including but not limited to cell banks, starting materials, raw materials, packaging materials, excipients.
Products which are either manufactured by a contract manufacturing organization for Boehringer Ingelheim or which are manufactured by Boehringer Ingelheim for a third party license holder.

* Changes to labels, artwork and regulatory product information will be implemented without a change according to this procedure if the change does not include any additional impact according to the defined scope above.

cells.text: An amendment to a change control is a controlled modification to the description, scope, justification or risk assessment of the change with repetition of the impact assessments and approval resulting in a modification of the required actions.
A planned permanent modification of a specified relevant item in scope of this procedure.

Formal process in order to ensure that a change to an item in scope of this procedure is described, justified, assessed, authorized, implemented and documented under the control of the relevant Quality unit.
A complete description of the proposed change, including the change scope/description, impact assessment, and action item plan.
The target date for the Final Approval of the change control. The date due must be extended before its expiration; if a due date extension is needed.

The effectiveness check is intended to confirm that the quality objectives of a change are achieved by the completion of the actions. Document the effectiveness either in the conclusions in step change summary or with a

separate effectiveness check after final approval and closure. A separate effectiveness check is requiredif further actions are required after implementation and closure of the change for the conclusive confirmation of the quality objectives e.g. IPC or batch release data of additional batches or further stability data. If the quality objectives cannot be finally confirmed further measures (e.g. further actions or new change controls) must be defined and carried out for either undo the change or finaly ensure the effectiveness of the change.

The date when the change is set up in production (e.g. new master batch record or new control variant of the testing specifications is approved and released, the changed application is installed in the production system and all tests are completed). The old set-up before the change was implemented cannot be used anymore.

A like-for-like change on equipment is documented in the corresponding logbook or equivalent accompanying record only. A regular change control process is not started provided that it affects an equivalent component with:
• No changed or applied additional functions
or specified technical procedure.
• Equivalent limits, forms, design and
specifications
• Same product-contacting material
No additional alteration of the component are required for its use

Changes can be classified depending on the nature, extent and potential impact. The following criteria for classification can be applied if not otherwise described in local procedures. Major change
• Changes with major impact on the quality of the process or product

• Changes with major impact on the existing validated status of the affected item
• Changes with an impact on the regulatory compliance, except for administrative changes
• Changes that require a GMP inspection by authorities Minor change
• Changes with minor impact on the process or product quality
• Changes with minor impact on the validated status of the affected item
• Changes without or only administrative impact on the regulatory compliance (e.g. name changes of suppliers) The classification from a regulatory point of view follows different criteria and is not described in this document.

A Master Change Control record is used in order to bundle single, interlinked change control records for the purpose of project management of changes and/or the unfeasibility to process a complex change in one change control.

A predefined change should be limited to minor changes and must not affect the regulatory compliance of submitted dossiers. The type of change must be defined in a Boehringer Ingelheim internal controlled document/record (e.g. SOP or AAP) together with its impact and the required actions. The approval is pre-achieved with the implementation of the controlled document/record. The change plan must be verified that it is in conformity to its reference. The performed actions and implementation are documented. For example, routine replacement actions could be defined in a local SOP, with documentation and testing reference included. The user may execute the preapproved “change plan” and document the results in a Pre-defined Change Control in GOTrack

Change that affects the manufacturing, packaging, quality control or distribution of a drug product, immunological, active pharmaceutical ingredient, excipient, intermediate, medical/administration device, drug device combination products or any component thereof including but not limited to solvents, raw materials, starting materials, packaging materials.

The release is intended to document and confirm that the change can be implemented without any remaining major nor critical risk. Document the release either with the final approval of the change or with a separate process step before change summary. The release can be granted for the entire change (complete) or for particular segments (partial release) according to the types below. It is approved by the Change Owner and Accountable Body with additional relevant stakeholder(s) as required.
1. Release for start of implementation The new set-up is prepared and tested in an environment, which is not in operational use. After the release for start of implementation is granted the new set-up is implemented into operational use, e.g., the changed application is installed in the productive environment or the changed master batch record is released.
2. Release for use in production
The new set-up is directly prepared in the environment for operational use (but not used before the release), e.g., for equipment changes.The release date is when the Quality Approval for the release is obtained.

Change includes the modification to any aspects of GxP equipment, facilities, utilities, computer systems, and/or spreadsheets. A technical change can be product- independent and as well be part of a product change that might be submission relevant.
Templates can be used to provide standardized information for changes, which can be imported into an actual change control. The management of the change control
templates must be described in the relevant global/divisional/local SOP, if utilized.

A temporary change control must neither be utilized for the immediate temporary remediation of an unforeseen event nor for the circumvention of defined quality processes nor for regulatory submission relevant product changes. A temporary change control is processed if a different set-up is planned to be used for a defined period before the following state is arranged. For the arrangement of the following state, either the change control for the temporary change is used by the inclusion of corresponding actions or an additional change control must be initiated accordingly.
The termination of a change control (cancellation of a change after change plan approval) is a controlled termination by approval including the controlled termination of the actions.
Unplanned and/or Emergency Occurrence (including Unplanned Change for Computer Systems)

In general a change control is defined as a process for deliberately chosen changes which are planned to be implemented in the future. Any unplanned and/or emergency occurrence is initially managed under the applicable global/divisional/local discrepancy process (events / deviations) including a root cause investigation and impact assessment for deviations. For Computer Systems only an unplanned/emergency change is always initiated as part of the incident process. It prevents the system from data loss or data integrity issues or returns the systems to an operating state by performing the required actions. In addition it ensures that the system will be returned into a validated state. For any other items in scope other than Computer Systems a regular change control might be initiated as part of the correction process, if required.

elements.text: GOTrack provides the possibility to use Template records for providing standardized information for changes, which can be imported into an actual change control record. The management of the change control templates must be organized by each individual area/function and must be described in the relevant global/divisional/local SOP, if utilized. The Template Owner is responsible for maintenance of the GOTrack templates in the relevant area/function.

GOTrack provides the possibility to use the Master Change Control record for bundling of single, interlinked change control records for the purpose of project management of changes and/or the unfeasibility to process complex changes in one change control process.

cells.text: This section describes the Predefined  Change Control process. Use this process for minor routine changes.

The type of change must be defined in a Boehringer Ingelheim internal controlled record together with its impact and the required actions. The approval is pre-achieved with the implementation of the Boehringer Ingelheim internal controlled record. A Predefined Change Control must not affect the regulatory compliance of  submitted dossiers.

For computer systems, the execution of all Predefined Changes (or Routine changes or Catalogue changes or Standard changes) managed by Boehringer Ingelheim have to be documented in GOTrack or in the IT Service Management tool. The corresponding AAP, TAP or SOP needs to define which tool (GOTrack or IT Service Management) is used. The process below describes the predefind change control process in GOTrack. The process in IT Service Management is governed by the corresponding SOP.
Change Control Process Definition of Predefined Change Control

Start a predefined change control if the planned change falls into the scope of this procedure and meets the conditions of a predefined change control in the relevant controlled document or electronic system.

• Make the reference to the relevant controlled
document or electronic system which defines the applicable predefine change.
• Define the responibilities

• Verify that the proposed predefined change meets
the conditions for a predefined change control in the referenced controlled document or electronic system
• Sign for verification
